message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long‑weekend holidays that occurred in Canada during 2023**.  
(“Long weekend” means the statutory holiday falls on a weekday and the adjacent weekend days give you a 3‑day break.  Where a holiday falls on a weekend, the weekend is already long, but it’s still noted for completeness.)

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| **Jan 1** | New Year’s Day | Sun | Jan 1–2 | Holiday on Sunday – weekend already long |
| **Feb 20** | Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, BC, Ontario) | Mon | Feb 18–20 | Creates a 3‑day break |
| **Mar 17** | St. Patrick’s Day (Newfoundland & Labrador) | Fri | Mar 17–19 | Province‑specific long weekend |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | Fri | Apr 7–9 | Creates a 3‑day break |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | Mon | May 20–22 | Creates a 3‑day break |
| **Jul 1** | Canada Day | Sat | Jul 1–2 | Holiday on Saturday – weekend already long |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | Mon | Sep 2–4 | Creates a 3‑day break |
| **Oct 10** | Thanksgiving | Mon | Oct 8–10 | Creates a 3‑day break |
| **Nov 11** | Remembrance Day | Thu | Nov 11–13 | Creates a 3‑day break |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas | Mon | Dec 23–25 | Creates a 3‑day break |
| **Dec 26** | Boxing Day | Tue | Dec 23–26 | Creates a 4‑day break (Christmas + Boxing Day) |

### Quick Takeaways

* **Family Day** (Feb 20) and **Victoria Day** (May 22) are the most common long‑weekend holidays across many provinces.  
* **Good Friday** (Apr 7) and **Remembrance Day** (Nov 11) also give you a 3‑day break.  
* **St. Patrick’s Day** is a holiday only in Newfoundland & Labrador, so only residents there get the long weekend.  
* **Canada Day** fell on a Saturday, so it didn’t create a new long weekend.  
* The **Christmas + Boxing Day** period gives a 4‑day break (Dec 23–26).

Feel free to plug these dates into your holiday‑planning app! If you need province‑specific holidays beyond the ones listed, let me know.
